newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank of Lebanon gross reserves rise in mid-Sept.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Lebanon gross reserves rise in mid-Sept.

text.p: Bank of Lebanon's gross foreign exchange reserves rose by $20.4 million in the first two weeks of September to $5,044.4 million, according to the central bank's bi-monthly balance sheet issued on Tuesday.
Gross reserves rose by $49.5 million in the second half of August to $5,024 million.
The central bank said the September increase was due to its purchases of foreign currency to safeguard monetary stability in Lebanon.
Gross reserves include commercial banks' foreign exchange deposits with the central bank.
The balance sheet did not give the Bank's net reserves, which were $2,858 million at the end of 1995 compared with $2,732 million at the end of 1994.
A banking source told Reuters on Tuesday that net reserves now totalled $3.5 billion. This compared with net reserves of $2.6 billion cited by the source at the end of May.
